Default decision thresholds for the adequacy call

Source: R/thresholds.R
defaultThresholds.Rd

Values used by callComparisons(), each from a validation experiment or a stated convention (threshold audit before 1.0.0); a user can override any.

Usage

defaultThresholds()

Value

A named list: cramerV (condition-covariate association above which a comparison is flagged Caution; on null splits with the confounder ignored, false discoveries rise above the base rate from 0.3), vif (variance inflation factor of the condition given the covariates at or above which the comparison is flagged Caution; a convention, R^2 = 0.8: adjusted fits stay calibrated and the power cost is already in the expected recall, but the estimate rests on the few samples that break the collinearity), sensitivity (expected recall at the target effect at or above which a comparison is adequately powered; 0.5 matches replication failure defined as recall below 0.5), minSamples (fewer samples per group is Invalid), cellsCondCor (absolute correlation of log cells per sample with condition above which cell-count imbalance is reported, and flagged Caution under DESeq2, whose FDR control it breaks), cellsCondAlpha (the correlation must also exceed the critical value at this level for the comparison's sample size, so chance correlations in small designs are not flagged: the cutoff is max(cellsCondCor, r_crit(n)), about 0.81 at 6 samples and cellsCondCor from ~16 samples), and minTestable (fewer testable genes is Underpowered; a convention guarding the genome-wide estimates behind the call, pi1 from BH discoveries and the dispersion prior; power stays calibrated down to 100-200 testable genes). The composition values (see assessComposition()) were calibrated on imposed subtype shifts in OneK1K (E6): compFDR (propeller FDR below which a child's share within its parent is called shifted), compFrac (expected DEGs from that shift alone, as a share of testable genes, at or above which the comparison is flagged Caution; 0.01 maximised Youden's J for predicting artefacts in at least 1% of genes, with no flags without a shift) and compExplained (share of a parent DEG's observed log2 fold change the predicted shift-only change must explain for the gene to be attributed to composition; 0.5: on natural age shifts in OneK1K (E5) it labels 3% of real within-subtype DEGs composition-driven, against 8% at 0.25, the best value on imposed shifts, while 0.99 of its composition-driven labels are artefacts).

Examples

th <- defaultThresholds()
th$sensitivity
#> [1] 0.5
# override one threshold, keep the rest
str(utils::modifyList(th, list(sensitivity = 0.7)))
#> List of 10
#>  $ cramerV       : num 0.3
#>  $ vif           : num 5
#>  $ sensitivity   : num 0.7
#>  $ minSamples    : num 2
#>  $ cellsCondCor  : num 0.5
#>  $ cellsCondAlpha: num 0.05
#>  $ minTestable   : num 200
#>  $ compFDR       : num 0.05
#>  $ compFrac      : num 0.01
#>  $ compExplained : num 0.5
